description: How the roles of the automated medication service relate to each other: care providers enroll patients and contract pharmacies, nurses monitor caseloads remotely, pouch rolls flow to homes, and adherence signals flow back.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Enrolling patients and contracting service partners

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Daily dispensing, monitoring, alarm response, and pouch supply

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Service fees and payment for the dispensing service

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Adherence signals, prescription changes, and safety reporting

relations.name: Enrolls patients onto the service
relations.description: Assesses which home-care clients are suitable for automated dispensing and onboards them, placing a device in the home and setting the personal dose schedule.

relations.name: Contracts dose dispensing
relations.description: Contracts the pharmacy to produce patient-specific multi-dose pouch rolls for the enrolled population and to keep production aligned with current prescriptions.

relations.name: Assigns caseloads and protocols
relations.description: Assigns clients to nurse caseloads and sets the alarm-response and escalation protocols that govern how missed doses are handled across the district.

relations.name: Supplies pouch rolls to the home
relations.description: Produces accurate, correctly sequenced pouch rolls and delivers them in time to be loaded into the patient's device before the previous roll runs out.

relations.name: Monitors doses and responds to alarms
relations.description: Watches the caseload remotely, follows up missed-dose alarms by phone or video, and drives to the home only when a dose situation cannot be resolved remotely.

relations.name: Signals adherence and alarms
relations.description: Every confirmed dispense and every missed or retracted dose flows from the home device into the nurse's caseload view as adherence data and safety alarms.

relations.name: Flags medication changes
relations.description: Passes prescription changes and dose-schedule updates observed in care to the pharmacy so upcoming pouch rolls match the current medication list.

relations.name: Reports safety and workload outcomes
relations.description: Feeds adherence rates, alarm volumes, and avoided home visits into the manager's safety and staffing KPIs that justify the service to the municipality.

relations.name: Pays the service fee
relations.description: Pays the monthly client fee or co-payment for the medication-dispensing service under the care provider's or municipality's charging scheme.
